# Scroll Area

A scrolling region with Koala's own scrollbar: an ink pill that overlays the content, shows while you are over it, fades rather than blinks, and looks the same on every OS and theme. The scrolling itself stays native.

```tsx
<ScrollArea fade className="h-72 w-72 rounded-lg shadow-xs ring-1 ring-edge">
  <div className="px-4 py-3">
    <h4 className="pb-1 text-sm font-semibold">Releases</h4>
    <List variant="plain">
      {releases.map((r) => (
        <ListItem key={r.version}>
          <ListItemContent>
            <ListItemTitle className="font-mono tabular-nums">v{r.version}</ListItemTitle>
          </ListItemContent>
          <ListItemMeta>
            <Badge variant={tone[r.tag]} size="sm">{r.tag}</Badge>
            {r.date}
          </ListItemMeta>
        </ListItem>
      ))}
    </List>
  </div>
</ScrollArea>
```

## Installation

```bash
# One-time setup (tokens + lib helpers)
npx koalaui-cli@latest init

# Add this component (its dependencies come along)
npx koalaui-cli@latest add scroll-area
```

Manual: run `npm install radix-ui tailwind-variants tailwind-merge`, then copy the source into `components/ui/scroll-area/` and adjust the import paths to your project. Components pull `cn` from `lib/utils`, the `tv` wrapper from `lib/tv`, and (for multi-part components) `createContext` from `lib/create-context`.

## Usage

```tsx title="usage.tsx"
import { ScrollArea } from "@/components/ui/scroll-area"

export function Example() {
  return (
    <ScrollArea className="h-72">
      {/* anything taller than 288px */}
    </ScrollArea>
  )
}
```

Give the root a height (`h-72`, `max-h-96`, or `flex-1 min-h-0` in a flex column) and the viewport fills it. `className` styles the root; the viewport inherits its radius, so a rounded frame clips the content and the focus ring to its corners.

## Edge fade

`fade` dissolves the edge that still has content beyond it, so the region says there is more before anyone hovers it. It is the `scroll-fade` utility, pure CSS: the edge you are scrolling toward fades, and the one you reach sharpens.

```tsx
<ScrollArea className="h-56">…</ScrollArea>
<ScrollArea fade className="h-56">…</ScrollArea>
```

## Horizontal

`orientation="horizontal"` draws the bar along the bottom and lets the content grow to its own width (`w-max` on the row). The photos sit 8px inside the frame, on 8px corners under its 16px ones, each with the thin image outline.

```tsx
<ScrollArea orientation="horizontal" fade className="max-w-lg rounded-lg shadow-xs ring-1 ring-edge">
  <div className="flex w-max gap-2 p-2 pb-4">
    {photos.map((photo) => (
      <figure key={photo.id} className="w-44 shrink-0">
        <div className="relative aspect-[4/3] overflow-hidden rounded-sm">
          <img src={photo.src} alt={photo.label} className="size-full object-cover" />
        </div>
        <figcaption className="px-1 pt-2 text-xs font-medium text-muted-foreground">{photo.label}</figcaption>
      </figure>
    ))}
  </div>
</ScrollArea>
```

## Both axes

`orientation="both"` draws both bars and a corner where they meet, for content wider and taller than its frame: a year of figures, a schedule, a canvas.

```tsx
<ScrollArea orientation="both" className="h-64 max-w-lg rounded-lg shadow-xs ring-1 ring-edge">
  <div className="px-4 py-1">
    <Table density="compact" className="w-max">…</Table>
  </div>
</ScrollArea>
```

## When the bar shows

`type` is Radix's: `hover` (the default) shows the bar while the pointer is over the region, `scroll` only while it is scrolling, and `always` whenever the content overflows. However it appears, it fades in and out, and it thickens a step when you reach for it, the way a native overlay bar does.

```tsx
<ScrollArea type="hover" className="h-40">…</ScrollArea>
<ScrollArea type="scroll" className="h-40">…</ScrollArea>
<ScrollArea type="always" className="h-40">…</ScrollArea>
```

## The viewport

`viewportRef` is the element that actually scrolls: read `scrollTop`, call `scrollTo`, or observe it. Here it drives a button that appears once you are away from the top and takes you back smoothly.

```tsx
const viewport = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)

<ScrollArea fade viewportRef={viewport} className="h-64">…</ScrollArea>
<Button size="sm" variant="secondary" onClick={() => viewport.current?.scrollTo({ top: 0, behavior: "smooth" })}>
  Back to top
</Button>
```

## API reference

### ScrollArea

The root, viewport, bars and corner in one. Props: `orientation` (`vertical` · `horizontal` · `both`), `fade`, `viewportRef`, plus Radix's `type` (`hover` · `scroll` · `always` · `auto`), `scrollHideDelay` (600ms) and `dir`. `className` goes on the root.

## FAQ

### Scroll Area or a plain overflow box?

The site's own scrollbars are hidden, so a plain `overflow-y-auto` box with the `scroll-fade` utility is the lighter option when the fade is cue enough: menus, pickers, chat logs. Use Scroll Area when the bar itself should show, for instance a long panel people drag through.

### Does it change how scrolling feels?

No. The viewport is a native scroller, so wheel, trackpad momentum, touch, keyboard and find-in-page all behave as usual. Only the bar is drawn by the component.

### Why doesn't my Scroll Area scroll?

It has no height to overflow. Give the root one: `h-72` or `max-h-96`, or `flex-1 min-h-0` inside a flex column, where `min-h-0` is what lets it shrink below its content.

### Why does `truncate` work inside a vertical area?

Radix wraps the content in a `display: table` box so a horizontal area can grow to its content. A vertical-only area puts that box back to a plain block, so truncation and long-word wrapping behave as they would anywhere else.

### Can a keyboard user scroll it?

Yes. The viewport is a native scroller: browsers let it take focus when nothing inside it can, and the arrow keys then scroll it. It shows an inset brand ring while focused.

## Exports and dependencies

`npx koalaui-cli@latest add scroll-area` writes `components/ui/scroll-area/`. Import from `@/components/ui/scroll-area`:

- Components and helpers: `ScrollArea`, `scrollAreaVariants`
- Types: `ScrollAreaProps`
- Koala lib helpers it uses: `tv`, `utils`
- npm packages: `radix-ui`
